question: Which of the following is a two carbon molecule?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ethanol**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ethanol, also known as ethyl alcohol, is a two-carbon molecule with the chemical formula C₂H₅OH.
 
• It is a common type of alcohol found in alcoholic beverages and is used as a solvent and in the manufacturing of various products.
 
• Ethanol is produced by the fermentation of sugars by yeasts or via petrochemical processes such as ethylene hydration.
 
• It is also used as a fuel additive in gasoline, known as bioethanol, to help reduce emissions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lactic Acid**

 
 
• Lactic acid is a three-carbon molecule with the chemical formula C₃H₆O₃.
 
• It is produced in muscle cells during intense exercise when oxygen levels are low, leading to anaerobic respiration.
 
• Lactic acid is also used in the food industry as a preservative and flavoring agent.
 
 
 
• **Pyruvic Acid**
 
 
• Pyruvic acid is a three-carbon molecule with the chemical formula C₃H₄O₃.
 
• It is an important intermediate in several metabolic pathways, including glycolysis and the citric acid cycle.
 
• Pyruvic acid can be converted into acetyl-CoA, lactate, or oxaloacetate depending on the cellular conditions.
 
 
 
• **Glucose**
 
 
• Glucose is a six-carbon molecule with the chemical formula C₆H₁₂O₆.
 
• It is a primary source of energy for cells and is involved in various metabolic processes.
 
• Glucose can be stored in the body as glycogen or converted into fats for long-term energy storage.
